title: Cash Application: What It Is and How to Automate It
summary: What cash application is, why it is hard, the step-by-step process, key metrics, and how AI agents automate matching payments to invoices.
body_markdown:
Getting paid is only half the battle. The other half is figuring out exactly which invoices a payment covers, so the books are right and customers are not chased for money they already paid. That matching process is **cash application** , and it is one of the most quietly painful jobs in accounts receivable, because the information needed to match a payment is so often incomplete.


This guide explains what cash application is, why it is hard, the process, the metrics that matter, and how AI agents automate it.


## **What is cash application?**


Cash application is the accounts receivable process of matching incoming customer payments to the open invoices they are paying, and recording them against the right customer accounts in the ledger. Done well, it keeps the AR subledger accurate, customer balances current, and collections focused on genuinely unpaid invoices. Done poorly, cash sits unapplied, balances drift, and customers get dunned for invoices they have already settled.


> A payment that lands in the bank is not really done until it is applied to the right invoices. Until then, it is just an unexplained deposit, and an unexplained deposit is a reconciliation problem waiting to happen.


## **Why cash application is hard**


- **Missing remittance.** Payments often arrive without clear remittance advice saying which invoices they cover.
- **Lump-sum payments.** A single payment may cover many invoices, sometimes partially.
- **Short pays and deductions.** Customers pay less than the invoice for discounts, disputes, or deductions that must be identified and coded.
- **Many formats and channels.** Payments come via ACH, wire, check, and card, with remittance spread across emails, portals, and attachments.


This is why cash application resists simple rules: matching the easy, clean payments is trivial, but the exceptions, which are common, require judgment.


## **The cash application process**


- **1. Receive the payment.** A payment lands via ACH, wire, check, or card.
- **2. Gather remittance.** Find the remittance advice, from the payment, an email, or a portal, that says what it is for.
- **3. Match to invoices.** Match the payment (and any deductions) to the open invoices it covers.
- **4. Handle exceptions.** Research short pays, overpayments, and unidentified payments.
- **5. Post and apply.** Record the payment against the customer account and clear the invoices.
- **6. Reconcile.** Confirm applied cash ties to the bank deposit.


## **Cash application metrics**


- **Auto-match rate.** The percentage of payments matched automatically without human touch, the headline efficiency metric.
- **Unapplied cash.** The amount of received cash not yet applied to invoices; lower is better.
- **Cash application cost per payment.** The labor cost of applying each payment.
- **Time to apply.** How quickly payments are applied after receipt, which affects the accuracy of[DSO](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/days-sales-outstanding) and collections.


## **How AI agents automate cash application**


Cash application is a classic case where AI goes beyond rules-based automation. ## **Frequently asked questions**


### **What is cash application?**


Cash application is the accounts receivable process of matching incoming customer payments to the open invoices they pay and recording them against the right accounts. It keeps the AR subledger accurate and ensures collections focus only on genuinely unpaid invoices.


### **Why is cash application difficult?**


Because payments often arrive without clear remittance, a single payment may cover many invoices, customers short-pay for discounts and deductions, and payments come through many channels and formats. Matching the clean payments is easy; the common exceptions require judgment.


### **What is a good cash application auto-match rate?**


Higher is better, and AI-driven cash application can push auto-match rates well above what rules-based matching achieves. The right target depends on your payment mix, but the goal is to minimize the payments that need manual research while keeping unapplied cash low.


### **Can cash application be automated?**


Yes. AI agents can read remittance from any format, match payments to invoices even when data is messy, code deductions, and research unidentified payments, applying clean matches automatically and surfacing only true exceptions, with every match traceable to source.


## **The bottom line**


Cash application is the unglamorous but essential work of matching payments to invoices so AR stays accurate and collections stay focused. It is hard because remittance is messy and exceptions are common, which is exactly why AI agents help: they match the messy cases, code the deductions, and leave only the true exceptions for a human, lifting the auto-match rate and freeing the team.
